differences.title: 1. INITIAL LOAD
differences.leftDesc: Zero JavaScript sent to client, leading to quicker initial page loads.
differences.rightDesc: Requires JavaScript download and execution, potentially delaying initial content display.

differences.title: 2. DATA FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Fetch data directly on the server, no extra client requests needed.
differences.rightDesc: Fetch data using hooks or lifecycle methods in the browser.

differences.title: 3. INTERACTIVITY
differences.leftDesc: Cannot use hooks like `useState` or `useEffect` directly.
differences.rightDesc: Can use all React hooks for dynamic user interactions.

differences.title: 4. CODE SIZE
differences.leftDesc: Reduces client-side JavaScript bundle size significantly.
differences.rightDesc: Includes all necessary JavaScript for rendering and interactivity.

differences.title: 5. SECURITY
differences.leftDesc: Sensitive API keys and logic remain on the server, not exposed to client.
differences.rightDesc: Client-side code is visible to users, requiring careful handling of secrets.

differences.title: 6. RENDERING LOCATION
differences.leftDesc: Components are rendered on the server before sending HTML to the client.
differences.rightDesc: Components are rendered in the user's browser after JavaScript loads.

differences.title: 7. DATA DIRECTLY
differences.leftDesc: Can directly access backend resources and databases without extra API calls.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on APIs or separate data fetching mechanisms to get data.
